frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Within the hamzated derivational family (the noun naba'/anbaa' plus the verbs nabba'a II, anba'a IV, istanba'a X), nbA contributes the authoritative disclosure to a recipient of a discrete, weighty/consequential REPORT - paradigmatically of the unseen (11:49 anbaa' al-ghayb), the absent/past (14:9, 9:70), the inner/concealed (9:64), or the coming outcome (6:67, 39:7) - together with the report so conveyed. The verb moves propositional content (marked by bi-) from a source that has it to a recipient who lacks it; the noun names that content. The nabiyy/anbiyaa'/nubuwwa nominal branch (weak third radical; nubuwwa realized with waaw, never a root hamza) is only THEMATICALLY associated with this nucleus (the prophet is the paradigmatic recipient of God's anbaa', 66:3, 11:49) and is NOT Quran-internally derived from it, so it is deliberately excluded from the confident claim.

The nabiyy/anbiyaa'/nubuwwa nominal branch (weak third radical; nubuwwa realized with waaw, never a root hamza) is only THEMATICALLY associated with this nucleus (the prophet is the paradigmatic recipient of God's anbaa', 66:3, 11:49) and is NOT Quran-internally derived from it, so it is deliberately excluded from the confident claim.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root splits into two branches that the packet merges under one root_id. The productive, hamzated branch means 'a weighty piece of news/report' (the noun naba') and 'to inform someone of such a report' (the verbs, forms II/IV/X). Its meaning is narrow and consistent: disclosing to a hearer content they could not otherwise reach - the unseen, the past, the hidden, the final outcome. The second, larger branch - nabiyy 'prophet' and nubuwwa 'prophethood' - is spelled with a weak radical (nubuwwa has a waaw, not a hamza) and is used as a fixed title; the Quran never internally derives 'prophet' from 'report,' so we keep the confident claim on the report/inform branch and mark the prophet branch as an unbridged, morphologically resistant seam.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: nbA(report/inform) is NOT: (a) mere speech or direct utterance - qawl/qala (13:33 opposes tunabbi'unahu to zahir min al-qawl); (b) teaching/imparting competence - 'allama (2:31-33 separates God teaching Adam the names from Adam's anba'a-ing them to the angels); (c) the act of narrating a sequence - qassa (11:100, 20:99, 7:101: qassa is the narrating, anbaa' the reported content); (d) the channel/text of revelation - wahy/kitab (11:49: anbaa' al-ghayb is the content revealed, distinct from the mode); (e) generic akhbar (9:94 distinguishes God's nabba'a-act from the akhbar it draws on). It does NOT entail the truth of what is conveyed (49:6 a fasiq brings a naba' requiring verification; 10:18, 13:33 ironic 'informing' God), nor the recipient's acceptance, nor restriction to past time (future/eschatological reports: 6:67, 38:88, 39:7). Weight/consequence is a strong DEFAULT, not a necessary condition (3:49 near-mundane content).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The nubuwwa tokens (57:26, 29:27, 6:89, 45:16, 3:79: 'wa-ja'alnaa fii dhurriyyatihi al-nubuwwata wa-l-kitaab') and the nabiyy/anbiyaa' singulars/plurals more broadly. Two independent blows: (1) MORPHOLOGY - the third radical of this whole branch surfaces as a weak semivowel; the abstract noun is spelled nubuwwa (waaw), not nubuu'a (hamza), so the Quran's own productive derivation treats it as a weak root distinct from the hamzated n-b-' of naba'/nabba'a; (2) SEMANTICS - nubuwwa sits in a bestowed-office frame (with al-kitab, al-hukm), carries zero 'report/tidings' content, and is never collocated with naba'/anbaa'. This branch is the PLURALITY of the root as delivered (80 of 160 tokens), so a single-nucleus claim would fail on the majority, not a fringe. This morphological seam is the reason the grade is capped at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE and the prophet branch is dispositioned STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY rather than folded into the nucleus.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: The 'announcement' unifier: read naba' as 'announcement,' nabba'a as 'announce,' and nabiyy as 'the announcer of God's message,' collapsing all 160 into one agentive sense and raising the grade toward STRONG/UNIVERSAL. Its best Quran-internal support is real and repeated: the Prophet is precisely the addressee who RECEIVES anbaa' (11:49, 3:44, 12:102 'anbaa' al-ghayb nuuhiihaa ilayka'), is commanded 'nabbi' 'ibaadii' (15:49), and 66:3 places nabiyy and nabba'a in one verse. It is rejected on Quran-internal grounds: (i) the text never uses nabiyy in an active announcing FUNCTION - that role is carried lexically by rasul/mubashshir/nadhir (33:45), never by nbA morphology behaving verbally; (ii) the verb's dominant agent is GOD, and naba' is brought by non-prophets (a hoopoe 27:22, a fasiq 49:6, mutually-inquiring people 33:20), so 'conveyer of naba'' does not single out the nabiyy; (iii) nubuwwa's waaw morphologically resists the hamzated root; (iv) unifying requires importing the inherited etymology 'nabi = announcer,' which the source policy forbids. Per 'prefer the narrowest defensible account,' the two-part account is preferred.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The 'announcement' unifier: read naba' as 'announcement,' nabba'a as 'announce,' and nabiyy as 'the announcer of God's message,' collapsing all 160 into one agentive sense and raising the grade toward STRONG/UNIVERSAL. Its best Quran-internal support is real and repeated: the Prophet is precisely the addressee who RECEIVES anbaa' (11:49, 3:44, 12:102 'anbaa' al-ghayb nuuhiihaa ilayka'), is commanded 'nabbi' 'ibaadii' (15:49), and 66:3 places nabiyy and nabba'a in one verse. It is rejected on Quran-internal grounds: (i) the text never uses nabiyy in an active announcing FUNCTION - that role is carried lexically by rasul/mubashshir/nadhir (33:45), never by nbA morphology behaving verbally; (ii) the verb's dominant agent is GOD, and naba' is brought by non-prophets (a hoopoe 27:22, a fasiq 49:6, mutually-inquiring people 33:20), so 'conveyer of naba'' does not single out the nabiyy; (iii) nubuwwa's waaw morphologically resists the hamzated root; (iv) unifying requires importing the inherited etymology 'nabi = announcer,' which the source policy forbids. internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses converge on a clean, distinctive hamzated report/inform nucleus spanning the naba' noun and the II/IV/X verbs: content is consequential and otherwise-inaccessible (unseen, past, inner, outcome), directionally disclosed knower->recipient, content marked by bi-; II and IV are Quran-internally interchangeable (66:3 'man anba'aka... nabba'aniya al-'aliim al-khabir'; 2:33 uses both), and X (10:53) is the request slot of the same nucleus - morphology != distinct meaning. The decisive division is the nabiyy/nubuwwa branch: Lenses A and B read it as a lexicalized offshoot bridged by usage; the adversary (C) shows the bridge is only thematic (no verse glosses or derives nabiyy via naba') and is morphologically resisted (nubuwwa in waaw, no root hamza anywhere in ~80 tokens), so unifying imports forbidden etymology. Aggregating honestly: the confident claim is scoped REPRESENTATIVE to the hamzated derivational family; the prophet/prophethood branch is retained in the partition but dispositioned STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY (an unbridged, morphologically distinct seam), which - being a resistant lexicalized nominal class that is in fact the plurality of tokens - caps the grade at MODERATE and forbids STRONG/UNIVERSAL. This forces neither a false unity (rejected) nor a nihilistic whole-root UNRESOLVED (the hamzated nucleus is genuinely well-evidenced).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: nabiyy/anbiyaa'/nubuwwa = prophet / prophethood, a lexicalized nominal branch. Its membership in the hamzated report/inform derivational family is NOT Quran-internally established.
clusters.classification_rationale: 80 tokens with a WEAK third radical (nabiyy in yaa', nubuwwa in waaw), never a root hamza. Fixed title in vocative/appositive frames (33:1, 65:1, 66:1; khaatam al-nabiyyiin 33:40; miithaq al-nabiyyiin 3:81) and the frozen polemic 'yaqtuluun al-nabiyyiin/al-anbiyaa' bi-ghayr al-haqq' (2:61, 2:91, 3:21, 3:112, 3:181, 4:155). nubuwwa clusters invariably with al-kitab/al-hukm as a bestowed office (6:89, 45:16, 3:79, 29:27, 57:26). No verse uses nabiyy as an active announcer or glosses it via naba'.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: The only link to the nucleus is thematic/contingent (the prophet as recipient of God's anbaa', 11:49, 66:3; command 15:49), never definitional or derivational; morphology (nubuwwa waaw) actively resists subsumption. Marked STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY - not RESISTANT (it does not contradict the nucleus) and not CONSISTENT (its derivation from the nucleus is undemonstrated and morphologically resisted).

reconciliation.rationale: The rhetorical impossibility trades on the very directionality it seems to break; it presupposes nabba'a = conveying putatively-unknown content, so it supports the nucleus.
Explicitly contrasted with 'zahir min al-qawl' - disclosure-of-the-real vs mere surface talk - so it strengthens rather than breaks the boundary.

occurrence_dispositions.note: 51 hamzated verb tokens. Dominant frame is the eschatological 'fa-yunabbi'ukum bi-maa kuntum ta'maluun' (6:60, 6:164, 5:105, 39:7, 62:8, passives 64:7, 75:13); same frame for dream-taawil (12:37, 18:78), hidden knowledge (9:64, 3:49), scripture (53:36). II and IV are interchangeable in one verse (66:3:24:1 anba'aka vs 66:3:27:1 nabba'aniya; 2:33 uses both) - morphology != meaning. X (10:53) inverts direction: seeking a naba' whose truth is at issue ('a-haqqun huwa').
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: nabba'a(II)/anba'a(IV)/istanba'a(X) = to disclose (or, X, to seek disclosure of) to a recipient content the recipient lacks, from a source of privileged knowledge; content marked by bi-.

occurrence_dispositions.note: 80 tokens with a WEAK third radical (nabiyy in yaa', nubuwwa in waaw), never a root hamza. Fixed title in vocative/appositive frames (33:1, 65:1, 66:1; khaatam al-nabiyyiin 33:40; miithaq al-nabiyyiin 3:81) and the frozen polemic 'yaqtuluun al-nabiyyiin/al-anbiyaa' bi-ghayr al-haqq' (2:61, 2:91, 3:21, 3:112, 3:181, 4:155). nubuwwa clusters invariably with al-kitab/al-hukm as a bestowed office (6:89, 45:16, 3:79, 29:27, 57:26). No verse uses nabiyy as an active announcer or glosses it via naba'.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: nabiyy/anbiyaa'/nubuwwa = prophet / prophethood, a lexicalized nominal branch. Its membership in the hamzated report/inform derivational family is NOT Quran-internally established.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: The only link to the nucleus is thematic/contingent (the prophet as recipient of God's anbaa', 11:49, 66:3; command 15:49), never definitional or derivational; morphology (nubuwwa waaw) actively resists subsumption. Marked STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY - not RESISTANT (it does not contradict the nucleus) and not CONSISTENT (its derivation from the nucleus is undemonstrated and morphologically resisted).

occurrence_dispositions.note: 51 hamzated verb tokens. Dominant frame is the eschatological 'fa-yunabbi'ukum bi-maa kuntum ta'maluun' (6:60, 6:164, 5:105, 39:7, 62:8, passives 64:7, 75:13); same frame for dream-taawil (12:37, 18:78), hidden knowledge (9:64, 3:49), scripture (53:36). II and IV are interchangeable in one verse (66:3:24:1 anba'aka vs 66:3:27:1 nabba'aniya; 2:33 uses both) - morphology != meaning. X (10:53) inverts direction: seeking a naba' whose truth is at issue ('a-haqqun huwa').
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: nabba'a(II)/anba'a(IV)/istanba'a(X) = to disclose (or, X, to seek disclosure of) to a recipient content the recipient lacks, from a source of privileged knowledge; content marked by bi-.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Directionality knower->non-knower is confirmed even by its ironic violation (10:18, 13:33 'informing' God), and the authority feature surfaces in 35:14 'wa-laa yunabbi'uka mithlu khabiir' and 66:3 'nabba'aniya al-'aliim al-khabir'.

Fixed title in vocative/appositive frames (33:1, 65:1, 66:1; khaatam al-nabiyyiin 33:40; miithaq al-nabiyyiin 3:81) and the frozen polemic 'yaqtuluun al-nabiyyiin/al-anbiyaa' bi-ghayr al-haqq' (2:61, 2:91, 3:21, 3:112, 3:181, 4:155). nubuwwa clusters invariably with al-kitab/al-hukm as a bestowed office (6:89, 45:16, 3:79, 29:27, 57:26). No verse uses nabiyy as an active announcer or glosses it via naba'.

occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: The only link to the nucleus is thematic/contingent (the prophet as recipient of God's anbaa', 11:49, 66:3; command 15:49), never definitional or derivational; morphology (nubuwwa waaw) actively resists subsumption. occurrence_dispositions.note: 51 hamzated verb tokens. Dominant frame is the eschatological 'fa-yunabbi'ukum bi-maa kuntum ta'maluun' (6:60, 6:164, 5:105, 39:7, 62:8, passives 64:7, 75:13); same frame for dream-taawil (12:37, 18:78), hidden knowledge (9:64, 3:49), scripture (53:36). II and IV are interchangeable in one verse (66:3:24:1 anba'aka vs 66:3:27:1 nabba'aniya; 2:33 uses both) - morphology != meaning. X (10:53) inverts direction: seeking a naba' whose truth is at issue ('a-haqqun huwa').
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: nabba'a(II)/anba'a(IV)/istanba'a(X) = to disclose (or, X, to seek disclosure of) to a recipient content the recipient lacks, from a source of privileged knowledge; content marked by bi-.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Directionality knower->non-knower is confirmed even by its ironic violation (10:18, 13:33 'informing' God), and the authority feature surfaces in 35:14 'wa-laa yunabbi'uka mithlu khabiir' and 66:3 'nabba'aniya al-'aliim al-khabir'.

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: naba'/anbaa' = a discrete, weighty/consequential REPORT whose truth-value is at stake, transmitted to a recipient - of past peoples, the unseen, or a coming outcome.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: The invariant is discrete propositional content, transmitted, consequential, with a truth-value that matters - not 'past news' and not generic akhbar (contrast 9:94).

independent_verification: Cross-checked across Lens A, Lens B, and adversarial Lens C on the same packet; all three independently isolate the same hamzated/weak-radical split and the nubuwwa-waaw morphological seam.
candidate_root_contribution: Within the hamzated derivational family (the noun naba'/anbaa' plus the verbs nabba'a II, anba'a IV, istanba'a X), nbA contributes the authoritative disclosure to a recipient of a discrete, weighty/consequential REPORT - paradigmatically of the unseen (11:49 anbaa' al-ghayb), the absent/past (14:9, 9:70), the inner/concealed (9:64), or the coming outcome (6:67, 39:7) - together with the report so conveyed. The verb moves propositional content (marked by bi-) from a source that has it to a recipient who lacks it; the noun names that content. The nabiyy/anbiyaa'/nubuwwa nominal branch (weak third radical; nubuwwa realized with waaw, never a root hamza) is only THEMATICALLY associated with this nucleus (the prophet is the paradigmatic recipient of God's anbaa', 66:3, 11:49) and is NOT Quran-internally derived from it, so it is deliberately excluded from the confident claim.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: Per-token QAC morphology and content-types: 29 hamzated naba'/anbaa' nouns, 51 hamzated verbs (46 II, 4 IV, 1 X), and 80 weak-radical nabiyy/nubuwwa nominals; verb content marked by bi- and drawn from unseen/past/inner/outcome domains.
layer_attribution.derivation: The hamzated noun naba' and the verbs nabba'a(II)/anba'a(IV)/istanba'a(X) form ONE derivational family (shared radicals, shared content-types, II~IV interchange at 66:3/2:33). The nabiyy/nubuwwa branch's derivation FROM this family is undemonstrated Quran-internally and is resisted by morphology (nubuwwa in waaw, no root hamza).
layer_attribution.lexical_class: nabiyy/anbiyaa'/nubuwwa are lexicalized as 'prophet'/'prophethood' - fixed titles, vocatives, and a bestowed office (with al-kitab/al-hukm), not transparently agentive 'announcer' items.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: The prophet is CONTEXTUALLY the paradigmatic recipient of God's anbaa' (11:49, 66:3) and is commanded to inform (15:49); this narrative/thematic association must NOT be promoted into the root claim as if it derived nabiyy from naba'.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Lenses A and B graded MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE derivational-family (prophet as lexicalized offshoot); adversary C argued whole-root UNRESOLVED on the unbridged, waaw-resisted seam. Aggregated: confident REPRESENTATIVE claim over the hamzated family; prophet branch retained as STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY, capping at MODERATE without forcing unity or collapsing the well-evidenced nucleus.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: Whether nabiyy/nubuwwa belong to the same root as naba'/nabba'a is UNRESOLVED: the branch is the plurality of tokens (80/160), is morphologically distinct (nubuwwa waaw), and has no Quran-internal derivational bridge - only a thematic one - so its membership is left open rather than asserted.

hard_cases.reason: nubuwwa realized with waaw in a bestowed-office frame (al-kitab), zero report content - the morphological/semantic seam against subsuming the prophet branch under the hamzated report nucleus.

evidence_basis.statement: nubuwwa is spelled with waaw (nubuwwa), not a root hamza (nubuu'a), so the Quran's own derivation treats the prophet branch as a weak root distinct from the hamzated n-b-' of naba'/nabba'a.

hard_cases.reason: nubuwwa placed in a lineage with al-kitab as a bestowed rank; no report/inform content.

evidence_basis.statement: nubuwwa is spelled with waaw (nubuwwa), not a root hamza (nubuu'a), so the Quran's own derivation treats the prophet branch as a weak root distinct from the hamzated n-b-' of naba'/nabba'a.

hard_cases.reason: nubuwwa coordinated with al-kitab and al-hukm as divine endowment; never collocated with naba'/anbaa'.

evidence_basis.statement: nubuwwa is spelled with waaw (nubuwwa), not a root hamza (nubuu'a), so the Quran's own derivation treats the prophet branch as a weak root distinct from the hamzated n-b-' of naba'/nabba'a.

hard_cases.reason: Vocative 'yaa ayyuha al-nabiyy' - a frozen lexicalized title with no recoverable 'report' content in situ; nabiyy in yaa', not a root hamza.

evidence_basis.statement: The prophet branch is used as a fixed title/name (weak radical) and is never used verbally as an announcer nor glossed via naba'; its link to the report nucleus is thematic, not definitional or derivational.

hard_cases.reason: al-nabiyy (weak radical) co-occurs in one verse with the hamzated verbs nabba'at/anba'a/nabba'a - the strongest apparent bridge, yet still only thematic (the prophet as one whom God informed), never a derivation of nabiyy from naba'.

evidence_basis.statement: 66:3 places nabiyy beside nabba'a/anba'a but only associates them thematically (the prophet is the one whom God nabba'a-ed); no verse derives or glosses nabiyy via naba', so the bridge is thematic, not Quran-internally definitional.

hard_cases.reason: A fasiq brings a naba' requiring verification - defeats any 'true/divine information' unifier for the report noun.

evidence_basis.statement: naba' does not lexically entail veracity: a corrupt person can bring one (49:6), so truth is contextually supplied, not carried by the lexeme.

hard_cases.reason: Ironic 'informing' God tests the directionality/veracity component of the verb.

evidence_basis.statement: nabba'a does not entail a true report: 10:18/13:33 apply it ironically to an empty pretension, so veracity is contextual, not lexical, while the knower->non-knower directionality is presupposed.

hard_cases.reason: Second ironic 'informing' God case, contrasted with mere surface talk.

evidence_basis.statement: nabba'a does not entail a true report: 10:18/13:33 apply it ironically to an empty pretension, so veracity is contextual, not lexical, while the knower->non-knower directionality is presupposed.

hard_case_representation.rationale: A genuine seam persists after reconciliation: the nabiyy/nubuwwa branch (80 tokens, the plurality of the root) is morphologically distinct (weak radical; nubuwwa in waaw) and is not Quran-internally derived from the hamzated report/inform nucleus, so it is retained in the partition but dispositioned STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY and represented here by its morphological seam (nubuwwa 57:26/29:27/6:89), its lexicalized title (33:1), and the strongest-but-still-thematic bridge (66:3). Adversarial boundaries within the confident branch (49:6 veracity; 10:18/13:33 directionality) are also recorded. The report/inform nucleus itself holds, so the whole root is not UNRESOLVED.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A verse in which nabiyy or nubuwwa is Quran-internally DERIVED from or glossed by naba'/anba'a - e.g. nabiyy predicated in situ as 'the one who conveys/receives a naba'' with report content recoverable from the token itself - which would license folding the prophet branch into the hamzated nucleus and upgrading the derivational-family claim.
rejection_condition.search_location: The 80 prophet-branch tokens in cluster C3, especially co-occurrence verses (66:3, 11:49, 15:49) and any predicative frame around nabiyy/anbiyaa'.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Check whether the nabiyy/nubuwwa token carries recoverable report/inform content in situ AND whether its third radical is hamzated; require a definitional (not merely thematic) link to naba'/nabba'a.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Reject thematic association (prophet happens to receive anbaa') as sufficient; exclude any reading that supplies the 'announcer' sense from inherited lexicon/etymology rather than from the Quranic token itself; do not treat the anbiyaa' plural -aa' as decisive since the afila' template supplies -aa' to weak-lam singulars too.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If no such internal derivation exists (expected), the prophet branch remains an unbridged, morphologically resistant seam, the claim stays REPRESENTATIVE/DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY over the hamzated family only, and the grade stays capped at MODERATE.

reopen_conditions: Reopen the merger if any verse derives or glosses nabiyy/nubuwwa via naba'/anba'a in situ (e.g. a nabiyy predicated as a conveyer/bearer of a naba' with recoverable report content), which would bridge C3 to the C1/C2 nucleus and warrant re-grading toward a single derivational family.

Reopen the morphological split if a naba'/anba'a-family token is found with a weak (yaa'/waaw) third radical, or if any nabiyy/nubuwwa token surfaces with a root hamza (e.g. nubuu'a instead of nubuwwa), collapsing the hamzated-vs-weak seam that currently separates C1/C2 from C3.

Reopen the 'prophet is not an announcer' boundary if istanba'a/anba'a/nabba'a is found with a nabiyy as the grammatical agent announcing to people (rather than God as agent and the prophet as recipient), which would let the report/inform function pick out the nabiyy.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: The hamzated report/inform nucleus (C1+C2, ~80 tokens) is adversarially clean and would independently support a strong result, but the prophet/prophethood branch (C3, ~80 tokens) resists the account (morphological seam, no internal derivation). Because the core holds while a coherent nominal sub-class resists, a full adversarial falsification is NOT_RUN over the whole root and the resisting occurrences are recorded here; the grade is capped at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE rather than being pushed to STRONG or collapsed to UNRESOLVED.
